title: fancy-sign: email one-time codes, their storage, their state transitions and the closed error-code set

contract.summary: Codes are six digits, stored only as HMAC-SHA256(app key, "envelope|signer|purpose|code"). Purposes view and accept are separate. A code expires after ttl_seconds (600), is consumed on use, and locks after max_attempts (5) wrong tries; a wrong try puts it back with one more attempt; a new request replaces the previous code. Sends are rate-limited per signer and purpose (5 per hour) and per IP. On the wire, an unknown, expired or wrong code is otp_invalid; only otp_locked is distinct. The otp.failed event records the precise reason (otp_unknown, otp_expired, otp_wrong). The accept code is checked LAST in sign, so a request refused for another reason burns nothing. See SPEC.md.

functions.errorCodes: errorCodes() -> {code: HTTP status}, the closed SignErrorCode set
functions.codeDigest: codeDigest({app_key, envelope_id, signer_id, purpose, code}) -> lowercase hex
functions.envelope: envelope({code, message, request_id}) -> the kit-wide error envelope body for one refusal: a 422 code as validation_failed with one item, every other code at the top level
functions.scenario: scenario({config?, steps}) -> {steps: [{op, result, events: [{type, source, data?}]}]}; data only for otp.* and link.* events. Steps: send | request {purpose, withSession?} | verify {code} | consent | open | advance {seconds} | sign {code} | changes {text} (0.53.0: request changes, answering {changes_requested}). A code is right (latest mailed), stale (the one before), wrong, view (the view code sent to sign) or six literal digits. One signer, alice, and a frozen clock.

contract.referenceNote: Goldens are particle-academy/fancy-sign's Signing service on its in-memory repository with a frozen clock and a capturing mailer, written by fancy-sign-php/tests/Conformance/Export.php.

notes: The scenario rows pin the redaction (one wire code, three recorded reasons), purpose binding, consumption, replacement, locking and the ceremony order. codeDigest is probed in tests/discrimination-sign.test.ts; the scenarios are not, because they need the whole service.
